items.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Chico O’Farrill wrote four of the arrangements for that. It was two big band sessions — one big band with two tunes, and then a smaller group, four horn things that he did with us.

ctx.x: Okay, I’ll have to get it to you. Chico O’Farrill wrote four of the arrangements for that. It was two big band sessions — one big band with two tunes, and then a smaller group, four horn things that he did with us. And I wrote a couple of things and Armando did the same. That’s a very nice album, “Havana Blues.” And that was it for that band. We’re still friends but we parted our ways. We teach now, together.
What are some of the things you learned as being a bandleader?
